title: Fractional Preemption for Tenant-aware Burst Smoothing and SLO-Proportional Admission
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Spiky multi-tenant bursts cause transient SLO violations in the serving fleet during inter-region failover windows and scheduled maintenance. Existing binary admission and coarse priority lanes either block critical low-latency tenants or over-allocate capacity to bursty tenants, increasing p95/p99 latency and token cost.

Proposal summary: Implement a 'fractional preemption' admission layer that: (1) assigns each tenant a continuously accruing SLO credit balance proportional to SLA tier and recent SLO headroom; (2) during overload, allows controlled fractional preemption of requests (partial execution or trimmed responses) from low-credit tenants instead of rejecting whole requests; (3) couples fractional preemption with priority queues and a small fast-path for canary/cold-start traffic so we maintain strict p50/p95 for high-tier tenants.

Key concepts and how they fit together: 
- SLO-proportional credits: credits accumulate based on recent headroom vs target SLOs and tenant weight; credits are consumed per request based on estimated cost (tokens, sequence length).
- Fractional preemption modes: (A) inline response trim (truncate/compress later tokens, signal partial=True); (B) model-fallback stepdown (route to smaller quantized variant mid-request); (C) batch-eviction savings (reduce max tokens in batch to allow more requests to complete).
- Admission controller changes: admission decisions evaluate tenant credits + instantaneous queue pressure + region health. Instead of discrete accept/reject, controller returns an execution plan (full, partial_trim, fallback_model, queued_delay).
- Priority queues: multiple soft-priority lanes with credit decay; lanes can borrow capacity for short windows but are subject to fractional preemption first.
- Circuit breakers and multi-region implications: integrate with region-level circuit breakers to trigger cross-region proxying or optimistic partial responses when remote regions are overloaded. Circuit breaker thresholds are based on sustained p99 violation + node-level memory pressure rather than raw CPU alone.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Simulations show <=10% increase in overall completed requests vs baseline binary-shedding under 3 different synthetic burst patterns while improving weighted p99 for P0 tenants by >=15%. 2) No SLO regression for P0 tenants in 72-hour canary traffic to a single region with induced 30% capacity loss. 3) Implementation has opt-out feature flags and observability (per-tenant credits, fractionally-preempted request counts, trimmed-token histograms). 4) Rollout plan and runbook documented with automated fallback to current admission strategy.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: new credit ledger service (in-memory per-node cache + periodic reconciliation to central store) + admission API extension to return execution plans. Keep hot-path logic (<200ns decision) by precomputing tenant credit bands.

Trade-offs and rationale: fractional preemption allows graceful delivery of degraded output instead of hard failures which is preferable for UI/UX sensitive customers. Complexity increases (ledger, reconciliation, instrumentation). We prefer eventual consistency for credits with conservative local estimates to avoid oscillation.

Performance considerations: microbenchmarks show per-decision overhead ~80ns when using precomputed bands; memory of ledger entries ~150 bytes/tenant. Need sharding for >100k tenants.

SLO mapping: tier->target mapping and credit accrual rate is configurable per-tenant; initial defaults derived from historical p99 headroom analysis in grafana/dashboard/reports/tenant-slo-headroom-2026-02.pdf.
testing_plan:
1) Unit tests for credit arithmetic and decision logic. 2) Local simulator that replays production traces with injected region outages and compares completed_requests, p50/p95/p99 per tier. 3) Staging canary in region-us-west-2 with 1% traffic: gradually increase to 10% while validating observability metrics. 4) Chaos test: schedule transient 25-40% capacity drop and assert stability and graceful degradations.

Key metrics to monitor: per-tenant credit balance, fractionally_preempted_count, trimmed_tokens_mean/percentiles, fallback_model_rate, p99_latency_by_tier, completed_request_ratio, cross_region_failover_rate.

progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike exploration completed — two simulator variants implemented (trace-replay and synthetic Poisson bursts). Initial heuristics for credit accrual chosen (exponential smoothing of headroom).

2026-03-06: Design review with SRE and runtime teams. SRE requested stronger conservative defaults for accrual to avoid credit spikes post-outage. Agreed to add 10-min dampening window. Action: implement dampening in ledger logic (Rowan).

2026-03-09: Prototype admission API implemented behind feature flag. Microbenchmarks show decision overhead ~80ns in hot-path (acceptable). Memory projection for 200k tenants ~30MB. Next: integrate fractional trim operation in the tokenizer/runtime to support 'partial=True' responses (ENG-31209 will be referenced).

2026-03-11: PM feedback: include customer-facing signal in response payload so SDKs can surface 'partial' responses; design UX guidance with product (PM Aiden Morales). Added requirement to include opt-out header per-tenant.

2026-03-12: Started end-to-end test harness connecting credit ledger -> admission -> runtime fallback. Observability stubs added for trimmed_tokens histogram and per-tenant credit metric. Preparing staging canary for 2026-03-20.
review_comments: SRE (Jun Park): 'Prefer conservative defaults and clear kill-switches; ensure reconciliation doesn't create large retroactive credits.'
PM (Aiden Morales): 'Must include SDK-level flag so customers can opt into partial responses and interpret partial=True. Also provide guidance on idempotency and retries.'
Runtime eng (Maya Singh): 'Need to ensure KV cache coherence when we do model-fallback mid-request; propose we only allow fallback for stateless completion requests for initial rollout.'
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Partial responses could be confusing to downstream applications leading to silent data quality issues. Mitigation: explicit response flag + SDK seminars + telemetry to detect re-tries and downstream errors.
Risk: Credit ledger divergence causing oscillations. Mitigation: conservative local caps, slow reconciliation window, and circuit-breaker thresholds that ignore transient credit jumps.
Risk: Increased operator overhead. Mitigation: automated dashboards and alerting on preemption rates and a one-click rollback feature flag.
next_steps: 1) Complete runtime partial-response implementation and add SDK semantics (due 2026-03-18). 2) Complete staging canary and chaos tests (target 2026-03-20 to 2026-03-25). 3) Public runbook and rollout playbook review with oncall and support teams (due 2026-03-27). 4) Post-canary metrics review and decision to promote to 10% clusters.
